keyRules: In Ukraine, during martial law, the civilian use of drones is prohibited—flights without military authorization are illegal.
An unidentified drone may be perceived as a threat. There is a real danger to life and safety—do not fly.

In exceptional cases, the police may use firearms to damage or destroy a drone if they reasonably believe it is being used to commit an offence or threatens people's life or health (Art. 46 of the Law "On the National Police").

Drone flights over state border crossing points, entry-exit checkpoints and State Border Guard Service facilities are prohibited; over the border strip as well, except in cases determined by the Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine (Art. 10 of the Law "On the State Border of Ukraine").
Disruptions to GPS and GNSS systems are frequently recorded near combat zones and in the Black Sea area. Never rely on satellite positioning.
Are you in Europe? This app shows the official airspace zones of 18 European countries—in Ukrainian.
We will update the app to provide full support on the same day that civilian flights are permitted again.
importantNotes: While martial law is in effect, information about Ukraine is limited to security-related data.
The State Aviation Service (Derzhaviavsluzhba) is the official source of information on aviation regulations in Ukraine.
Ukrainian citizens can register as drone operators in an EASA member state and legally operate drones throughout the EU.
